_comment: T-0099: the live-conflict pages. Hand-picked objects per conflict (matrix first, then candidates the editor approves), the stakes, and the object that marks the day the clock starts, if there is one. build_backstory.py reads this; an object shows only if it is in the matrix or approved in the candidates workbook, with a live link. Text for each object is in object-notes.json (verified: false until the editor checks it).

ukraine-russia.stakes: The open question is whether a border agreed in treaties holds when a larger neighbour decides it does not. It also asks who guarantees a smaller country's security, and what Russia, Ukraine and their backers will each accept to end the fighting.

gaza.stakes: The open question is whether force can secure Israel's south and bring the hostages home, and at what cost to Gaza's civilians. It also asks who governs Gaza when the fighting stops, and whether any arrangement can satisfy both Israeli security and Palestinian self-rule.

israel-hezbollah.stakes: The open question is whether Israel's northern border can be quiet while an armed group outside the Lebanese state holds weapons on the other side. It also asks who disarms Hezbollah, and whether Lebanon's army and government can take control of the south.

us-israel-iran.stakes: The open question is whether strikes can stop Iran's path to a nuclear weapon, or only delay it while widening the war. It also asks who decides when American force is used, and what would bring Iran, Israel and the United States to a lasting halt.

us-canada-trade.stakes: The open question is whether tariffs between neighbours with deeply joined economies win concessions or mostly raise costs on both sides. It also asks who bears those costs, and whether the trade agreement that binds North America survives its next review.

sudan.stakes: The open question is whether two armies that each claim to be the state can be brought to a settlement, or whether Sudan breaks apart. It also asks who protects civilians in Darfur and elsewhere, and which foreign backers keep the war going.

venezuela.stakes: The open question is whether a state emptied by economic collapse and emigration can be rebuilt after Maduro's removal by foreign force. It also asks who holds legitimate authority now, and whether the millions who left will come back.
